finding.title: Guard FirebaseAuthGatewayImpl link/reauth methods against silent no-op on null currentUser
finding.why: If currentUser is null when these fire (expired/revoked anonymous session, or a UI race), the `?.` swallows the call and the method returns a normally-completed Future<void> — no exception, no signal that nothing happened. The one real caller (features/account/data/repositories/auth_repository_impl.dart:129-140 `linkGoogleProvider`/`linkEmailProvider`/`reauthenticateWithGoogle`) just awaits and reports success with nothing to double-check. That directly undercuts AU-1: linking must actually run against the anonymous uid so its offline data carries over; a silent no-op leaves the account anonymous while the user believes it's now permanent, and Identity Platform auto-deletes unlinked anonymous accounts after 30 days (AU-3's rationale), which can permanently orphan the child's offline learning history. Every sibling precondition check in this same file (deleteCurrentUser:172-176, updatePassword:181-186, reauthenticateWithEmail:192-199, sendEmailVerification:100-104) throws `StateError` instead of silently no-op'ing; the one genuinely-intentional no-op in the file (`updateDisplayName`) is declared as such by an explicit 'is a no-op when no user is signed in' test — these three methods have neither the guard nor a test declaring the no-op intentional, which is the tell that it's an oversight, not a design choice.
finding.recommendation: Add the same `if (user == null) throw ...` guard used elsewhere in this file before calling linkWithCredential/reauthenticateWithCredential in all three methods (ideally throwing the typed exception recommended in the companion EH-5 finding rather than another StateError). Add regression tests mirroring the existing 'throws when no user is signed in' pattern for linkWithGoogleIdToken, linkWithEmailAndPassword, and reauthenticateWithGoogleIdToken.
acceptance_criteria: linkWithGoogleIdToken, linkWithEmailAndPassword, and reauthenticateWithGoogleIdToken throw (not silently no-op) when currentUser is null.
New red-first unit tests in firebase_auth_gateway_impl_test.dart cover the null-currentUser case for all 3 methods and pass.
Existing 'links credential when signed in' tests for the same methods stay green.
